proposed_fix.description: Relieve CPU pressure on ts-order-service by first confirming where the CPU is going, then adding capacity (gated, reversible), and only with human approval.
steps: Capture a CPU profile or thread dump from one ts-order-service pod to identify hot code paths (read-only).
Compare the start of the CPU/latency rise against recent deploys, config changes, or traffic shifts for ts-order-service.
Check the CPU requests and limits and any throttling on the pods, to see whether the limit is too low for the current load.
If CPU is saturated and load is legitimate, scale ts-order-service out by a small increment (e.g. +1 or +2 replicas) after human approval, and watch latency-50 and CPU for several minutes.
If a recent deploy or config change correlates with the onset, propose rolling that change back as a separate, human-approved action.

Check the downstream services that also show elevated latency (ts-preserve-service, ts-security-service, per E1) after the order-service change, to confirm they recover and were only affected as callers.
preconditions: Confirm that the cluster has spare capacity for additional replicas.
Confirm that ts-order-service's current replica count and autoscaler settings are known and recorded, so they can be restored.
Confirm the CPU rise is not caused by an expected load event such as a batch job or load test.
Get on-call approval before any scaling or rollback is executed.
proposed_fix.rollback: Scale ts-order-service back to the originally recorded replica count (and restore the original autoscaler or resource settings if they were changed); if a deploy rollback was performed, redeploy the previous version. Diagnostic captures need no rollback.
